newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude pegged back by late profit taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude pegged back by late profit taking.

text.p: IPE Brent crude fell rapidly at the close on late proft taking after recovering from and early afternoon fall led by weaker NYMEX markets, traders said.

March Brent last traded down 54 cents at $22.54 one cent off the day's low. Trade was choppy. The market had barely recoved from a mid-afternoon slump as sharp early losses on NYMEX products triggered bouts of stop loss selling, before e profit taking pegged it back again at the close.
The front month contract has lost $1.97, trading down to a low of $22.56, since the high last week of $24.91, which itself was close to the six-year peak of $25.06 from October.
"Trade was choppy, there's nothing fundamental out there it's just technically weaker," said a trader.
February gas oil futures last traded down $3 on Friday after recovering in sympathy with crude from the NYMEX products inspired early afternoon fall.
The contract finished at $215.75 a tonne, after toucing $214.75 in mid-afternoon.
"Gas oil followed crude higher, helped by the widening Feb/March spread on WTI," a trader said, adding activity in the gas oil contract was thin and mainly local.
However, traders expected to see further losses on Monday in catch-up to late weakness on The NYMEX heating oil market.
